extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI)
extraction.description: A multimodal benchmark comprising 20,000 conflicting instructions across 8 tasks, evenly distributed between language-language and vision-language paradigms, designed to evaluate the capability of large multimodal models to recognize and detect self-contradictory instructions.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, Dequan Wang
extraction.publisher: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Fudan University, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created using AutoCreate, an automatic dataset creation framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) and programs. AutoCreate starts from manually input seeds and maintains a seed pool, using a generator-decorator-cleaner pipeline in iterative cycles to produce language-language and vision-language self-contradictory instruction data. Both human experts and LLMs are involved in quality checking.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of manually input seeds for language tasks, and for vision-language tasks, raw visual-language data is generated via programs and LLMs. SemanticConflict additionally uses the ImageNet dataset as an external source for images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human experts rigorously checked the quality of the AutoCreate-generated dataset. Both human experts and LLMs are involved in double-checking the quality of the generated dataset. Subsets (SCI-Core, SCI-Base) are selected manually. For V-L tasks, evaluation is conducted by both human experts and three LLMs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Correlation coefficients from GPT-4 are presented; evaluation agents include ChatGPT, ChatGLM, and human experts for V-L tasks to assess consistency.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Large Language Models (LLMs) including GPT-4, ChatGPT, and ChatGLM were used as automated generators, decorators, cleaners, and quality checkers in the AutoCreate framework.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark only includes language-language and vision-language paradigms, lacks fine-grained control to determine conflict degree, and does not provide a detailed study on the attention mechanism of large multimodal models when confronted with conflict instructions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The SCI benchmark provides a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction. It promotes inclusivity in AI research through diverse instruction datasets, enhances context-aware understanding, and fosters trust and reliability in AI systems essential for societal integration.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) on their ability to detect conflicting/self-contradictory instructions across language-language and vision-language paradigms. It supports qualitative evaluation via three splits (SCI-Core 1%, SCI-Base 10%, SCI-All 100%) and is used for benchmarking 5 language and 6 vision-language models.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to include more modalities in future versions of the SCI benchmark using the AutoCreate framework.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset is split into three subsets (SCI-Core, SCI-Base, SCI-All) selected manually at 1% and 10% of SCI-All. Images are augmented with variation in font, size, and color. For FigureConflict, numerical data is manipulated by changing the maximum value to the minimum value. For SemanticConflict, correct labels are substituted with similar but different objects.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data is generated using the AutoCreate framework with a generator-decorator-cleaner pipeline. The Generator creates initial language/vision data, the Decorator introduces self-contradictions, and the Cleaner removes data not meeting quality standards. Both human experts and LLMs double-check quality. High-quality data is refined to extract new seeds for the seed pool.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: AutoCreate requires a small batch of manually input seeds to automatically generate a large quantity of high-quality, diverse data by Large Language Models (LLMs). Specifically, in a single iteration, the generation process comprises two loops: the Language Loop (left) and the Visual Loop (right). Each loop originates from the Seed Pool and is sequentially processed by a fully automated Generator, Decorator, and Cleaner, culminating in a high-quality dataset production.
